goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points to the same problem: getSubGroupsCount returning null breaks the GroupModel contract, which says it never returns null, and can cause NPEs.

goldens.comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
goldens.reasoning: Both point to the reader thread never being joined, which is the same root problem. The golden says this makes the test flaky because exceptions can be missed. C2 says the thread could hang instead, which is a different consequence of the same defect.

candidates: GroupAdapter#getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the delegate group is concurrently missing, violating the GroupModel contract (never null) and causing NPEs via auto-unboxing in admin endpoints/tests that expect a numeric count

The new concurrency test starts a background thread that is never joined and only stops when a flag is set after deletions - if deletions throw or the read call blocks, the thread can run indefinitely and hang the test JVM
The read loop in the concurrency test has no backoff/sleep, causing busy-spin at high CPU
